channel.description: Latest articles from UK Defence Journal (ukdefencejournal.org.uk)

item.title: UK to restart nuclear submarine defuelling in 2026
item.description: The Ministry of Defence has confirmed that defuelling of the UK’s decommissioned nuclear-powered submarines is set to restart in 2026, as preparations continue at specialist dock facilities in Devonport. The post UK to restart nuclear submarine defuelling in 2026 first appeared on UK Defence Journal.

item.title: MOD cites family life and civilian jobs in troop exits
item.description: The Ministry of Defence has said that pressures on family life and opportunities outside the military remain the primary reasons personnel leave the armed forces, despite recent improvements in recruitment and retention. The post MOD cites family life and civilian jobs in troop exits first appeared on UK Defence Journal.

item.title: UK Government has sought ‘legal advice’ on Ajax
item.description: The Ministry of Defence has confirmed that it has sought legal advice from the Government Legal Department on the troubled Ajax armoured vehicle programme, following a direct question from Mark Francois MP. The post UK Government has sought ‘legal advice’ on Ajax first appeared on UK Defence Journal.

item.title: RAF Voyager tankers and Typhoon jets scramble for Arctic
item.description: RAF Voyager tankers and Typhoon jets have been scrambled to support an inbound cargo aircraft, expected to enter UK airspace precisely at midnight tonight. The post RAF Voyager tankers and Typhoon jets scramble for Arctic first appeared on UK Defence Journal.

item.title: What Formula 1 can teach defence about wartime pace
item.description: Drawing on experience from Formula 1 and his work at PurpleSector, Mark Mathieson MBE argues that defence can learn practical lessons from high performance engineering as it seeks to operate at wartime pace in peacetime. The post What Formula 1 can teach defence about wartime pace first appeared on UK Defence Journal.

item.title: NATO sets out layered security guarantees for Ukraine
item.description: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte has set out a three-layer approach to long-term security guarantees for Ukraine, arguing that any future peace settlement must ensure Russia is unable to launch renewed aggression. The post NATO sets out layered security guarantees for Ukraine first appeared on UK Defence Journal.

item.title: Troops remain on duty over Christmas
item.description: Around 19,000 British Armed Forces personnel will remain on duty or on standby over the Christmas period, including large numbers based in Scotland, as the UK maintains military readiness at home and overseas. The post Troops remain on duty over Christmas first appeared on UK Defence Journal.

item.title: MP hails Babcock workforce at Rosyth
item.description: At the keel laying of the Royal Navy’s third Type 31 frigate, HMS Formidable, Dunfermline and Dollar MP Graeme Downie delivered a speech that doubled as a tribute to Rosyth’s workforce and a quiet strategic warning about the world these ships are being built for. The post MP hails Babcock workforce at Rosyth first appeared on UK Defence Journal.

item.title: Britain looking at rolling out laser weapons across forces
item.description: The Ministry of Defence has confirmed that it is continuing to explore directed energy weapons across multiple domains. The post Britain looking at rolling out laser weapons across forces first appeared on UK Defence Journal.

item.title: British forces deployed worldwide on Christmas Day
item.description: Thousands of British Armed Forces personnel will remain deployed or on standby across the globe on Christmas Day, continuing operations that span Europe, the Middle East, the Indo-Pacific, Africa, the Caribbean, British Overseas Territories and the UK itself. The post British forces deployed worldwide on Christmas Day first appeared on UK Defence Journal.
